title: Coherent ends and cellular weighted limits of enriched categories
statement:
Use universes, quasicategories, coherent diagrams and transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], complete algebroids of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the tensor, internal functor category, free enrichment and cotensor conventions of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably closed symmetric monoidal infinity-category, with unit $\mathbf1$ and internal Hom $[v,-]$. Write $U\mathcal E$ for the category underlying a complete $\mathcal V$-category $\mathcal E$, with mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\mathbf1,\mathcal E(x,y))$.

Let $J$ be a small simplicial category and $W:J\to\mathsf{sSet}$ a simplicial functor. Call $W$ cellular if $\varnothing\to W$ is a small transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of maps $J(j,-)\times\partial\Delta^n\to J(j,-)\times\Delta^n$, for $j\in J$ and $n\geq0$. Let $F:J\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ be a diagram retaining enriched functors, enriched transformations and their higher simplices, represented by a strict simplicial functor into a compatible enriched simplicial presentation as explicitly defined and supplied by [lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation]. Then the cellular weighted limit $\{W,F\}_J$ exists as a complete $\mathcal V$-category. Its underlying category is naturally equivalent to the simplicial weighted limit $\{W,UF\}_J$, whose $r$-simplices are simplicial natural maps $W\times\Delta^r\to UF$. This comparison retains all transformation simplices and is compatible with evaluation and maps of cellular weights.

In the cellular construction, a generating weight $J(j,-)\times S$ gives the cotensor $F(j)^S$; a pushout attaching cells gives a pullback, coproducts give products, and continuous composites give inverse limits. Mapping objects at a limit of enriched categories are the corresponding limits of mapping objects at compatible objects. For a small infinity-category $S$ and coherent diagrams $P,Q:S\to U\mathcal E$, the mapping object of the cotensor is the coherent end
$$\mathcal E^S(P,Q)\simeq\lim_{(s\to t)\in\operatorname{Tw}(S)}\mathcal E(Ps,Qt).$$
Here $\operatorname{Tw}(S)$ and its source-target map are [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]; the diagram uses precomposition and postcomposition, and retains their coherent compatibilities. For simplicial shapes use their freely generated infinity-categories. All these mapping-object formulas preserve evaluation, identities, composition and additional coherent parameters. The functor $[v,-]$ preserves all the small limits appearing in these formulas. No tensoring of objects of the individual categories $F(j)$ is assumed.

For every complete $\mathcal V$-category $\mathcal B$, the evaluation cone induces an equivalence of complete enriched functor categories
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal B,\{W,F\}_J)\simeq\{W,\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal B,F(-))\}_J.$$
The right side is formed by the same cellular construction. Underlying it is the simplicial category of strict enriched $W$-cones with vertex $\mathcal B$: its $r$-simplices are natural maps $W\times\Delta^r\to U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal B,F(-))$. The equivalence retains enriched transformations and higher simplices and commutes with evaluation, composition in $\mathcal B$ and changes of cellular weight. In particular a strict enriched $W$-cone in the full functor categories gives an enriched functor to $\{W,F\}_J$, without assuming any of the $F(j)$ are tensored.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1--5.1.8 and 5.2.2--5.2.9, cellular weighted-limit calculus; agent-formulated enrichment transfer and coherent-end refinement using Haugseng, On the tensor product of enriched infinity-categories, Remark 9.5, and the complete-algebroid limit construction. These combined refinements are not a theorem quoted verbatim from Riehl--Verity. Sources read online; archival copies WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched infinity-categorical assertion. Repair: the presentation is now defined in its own node, and the enriched functor-category weighted-limit universal property is stated explicitly.

proof.text: First record the limit comparisons needed below. The free-enrichment adjunction in [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] makes $U$ preserve small limits: applying its mapping-space adjunction to a test category $K$ identifies maps $K\to U\lim E_i$ with $\lim_i\operatorname{Map}(K,UE_i)$. The representable criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies this with $\lim_iUE_i$. The same argument with a test enriched category $T$ and the tensor-Hom adjunction gives $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,\lim E_i)\simeq\lim_i\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,E_i)$ as complete enriched categories: both sides represent $T\mapsto\lim_i\operatorname{Map}(T\otimes B,E_i)$. Thus the comparison concerns internal functor categories, not only their cores. The cotensor clause of the tensor calculus gives $U(E^S)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(S,UE)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,E^S)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,E)^S$. These equivalences are the evaluation comparisons.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text: For any strict simplicial diagram $A:J\to\mathsf{qCat}$ put $C_W(A)_r=\operatorname{Nat}_J(W\times\Delta^r,A)$. A map $J(j,-)\times S\times\Delta^r\to A$ restricts at $1_j$ to $S\times\Delta^r\to A(j)$; its inverse sends $(\alpha,s,t)$ to $A(\alpha)(s,t)$. Naturality and the identity law make these inverse in every degree. Hence $C_{J(j,-)\times S}(A)=A(j)^S$. A natural map out of a pushout of weights is exactly a pair of maps agreeing on its common subweight; this statement holds after multiplying by every $\Delta^r$, since products of simplicial sets preserve colimits degreewise. Thus weight pushouts become simplicial pullbacks, coproducts become products, and continuous unions become inverse limits. This is the explicit weight calculation; it makes no claim that arbitrary strict pullbacks are homotopy pullbacks.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text:
Fix the small cellular filtration $(W_\alpha)_{\alpha\le\lambda}$. By transfinite induction construct complete $\mathcal V$-categories $L_\alpha$ with transition functors and prove the invariant $I_\alpha$: for every complete $\mathcal V$-category $B$, in a presentation obtained by [lem-coef-presentation-enlargement-retains-diagram] (applied once or twice) containing $B$, $L_\alpha$, the completed enriched tensor unit $I$, the required internal functor categories and cotensors, and retaining the original strict $F$ literally, put $A_B(j)=\mathscr P(B,F(j))$; there is a comparison
$$\Phi^\alpha_B:U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,L_\alpha)\simeq C_{W_\alpha}(A_B),$$
natural in $B$ under precomposition with enriched functors $B'\to B$ (computed in an enlargement containing both). Its evaluation cone is $e_\alpha=\Phi^\alpha_{L_\alpha}(\mathrm{id})\in C_{W_\alpha}(A_{L_\alpha})$; by naturality $\Phi^\alpha_B(g)$ is $e_\alpha$ composed with $g$. Carry these comparisons together with the specified hom-quasicategory and cotensor identifications of [lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation], including evaluation maps, so the induction concerns whole diagrams and boundary families. Each $B$ is fixed before enlarging; no one presentation contains every $B$. Also run the induction on the strict map $A_I\to U_{\mathscr P}F$ obtained by evaluating the strict forgetting functor at a chosen object of $U_{\mathscr P}I\simeq UI$ (which need not be contractible: for $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ its endomorphism monoid is $\mathbf Z$). It is strictly natural; its components correspond to $U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(I,F(j))\simeq UF(j)$, the unit equivalence of the closed symmetric monoidal tensor calculus, hence are equivalences. For the empty weight take the terminal enriched category; all cone simplicial sets are terminal, so $I_0$ holds.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text: For each small family of attaching cells, the strict products of the quasicategories appearing in step 2 compute products in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Indeed, well-order the family, start at $Q_0=*$, put $Q_{\gamma+1}=Q_\gamma\times_*D_\gamma$, and take the degreewise inverse limit at every nonzero limit ordinal. The successor projection is an isofibration: lift each inner horn and each equivalence in its new $D_\gamma$ coordinate. By [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] the successor square is a categorical pullback, and by [lem-coef-transfinite-isofibration-limit] each continuous tower limit is a categorical limit. This identifies the final degreewise product with the categorical product, including the empty family. A product of the boundary restrictions $A(j)^{\Delta^n}\to A(j)^{\partial\Delta^n}$ is an isofibration: the factor restrictions are isofibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], and their horn and equivalence lifts can be chosen coordinatewise. This argument applies to every diagram model used in the induction. Step 1 identifies the corresponding enriched products after applying $U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,-)$.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text:
Suppose the next cells have labels $(j_a,n_a)$. Restricting the evaluation cone $e_\alpha$ of step 3 along their attaching maps and applying the cotensor adjunction gives
$$L_\alpha\longrightarrow\prod_a F(j_a)^{\partial\Delta^{n_a}}.$$
Form in $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ the pullback
$$L_{\alpha+1}=L_\alpha\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\prod_aF(j_a)^{\partial\Delta^{n_a}}}\prod_aF(j_a)^{\Delta^{n_a}}.$$
Step 1 computes its image under $U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,-)$ as the corresponding categorical pullback. On the strict cone side step 2 gives the degreewise pullback, whose boundary-restriction leg is an isofibration by step 4. Hence [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] identifies that pullback with the categorical pullback. The hom-quasicategory, cotensor and evaluation identifications in [lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation], together with $\Phi^\alpha_B$, identify these cospans including the attaching maps: by the naturality in $I_\alpha$, $\Phi^\alpha_B$ carries postcomposition with the attaching functor, which is the restriction of $e_\alpha$, to restriction along the specified maps into $W_\alpha$. Applying the pullback universal property gives $\Phi^{\alpha+1}_B$, natural in $B$ because every map used is postcomposition or restriction; this gives $I_{\alpha+1}$. For the strict map $A_I\to U_{\mathscr P}F$, its equivalences give equivalences on the two cotensor products; the same cospan argument gives an equivalence on the next cone categories. The comparisons retain every simplex because all these operations occur in whole quasicategories. This is the successor step of the simultaneous induction, including $n_a=0$ with empty boundary.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text:
At a nonzero limit ordinal $\beta$ put $L_\beta=\lim_{\alpha<\beta}L_\alpha$. Step 1 computes $U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,L_\beta)$ as the categorical limit of its earlier values. For each strict diagram $A$ in the induction, step 2 gives $C_{W_\beta}(A)=\lim_{\alpha<\beta}C_{W_\alpha}(A)$ degreewise. Successor restrictions are pullbacks of the isofibrations of step 4, and limit stages are exactly continuous by this equality. Thus [lem-coef-transfinite-isofibration-limit] identifies each strict tower limit with its categorical limit. The preceding comparisons commute coherently with every projection, since they were constructed from evaluation and its restrictions at successor stages. Taking their limits gives the comparisons at $\beta$, including the comparison between the $A_I$ and $U_{\mathscr P}F$ towers. To see that these limit comparisons are equivalences, take the limit of their inverse equivalences and inverse homotopies; the projection identities give both inverse identities. This uses only the definition of equivalence and functoriality of the limit universal property, not a rectification or cellular-transfer theorem. Induction gives $L=L_\lambda$ and
$$UL\simeq U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(I,L)\simeq C_W(A_I)\simeq C_W(U_{\mathscr P}F).$$
The last diagram is the retained strict representative of $UF$. Every ordinal, family and limit is small in the stipulated universe.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text: For any complete $B$, step 1 identifies the cellular construction after applying $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,-)$ with the same enriched construction on $j\mapsto\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,F(j))$: this holds on generating cotensors and on every product, pullback and inverse limit. The simultaneous induction of steps 3--6 identifies its underlying category with $C_W(A_B)$, using the presentation's specified whole hom-quasicategory comparisons for $U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,F(-))$. In particular their attaching maps agree under those comparisons as checked in step 5; no separate transfer from a merely objectwise equivalent diagram is invoked. At each cell the comparison is evaluation followed by currying, and at attachments and limits its projections are those maps. It is therefore the equivalence induced by the evaluation cone. Coherent currying and evaluation in [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] give compatibility with composition in $B$. Restricting a cone along $W'\to W$ gives a cone over $W'$ with vertex $L$; the established comparison for $B=L$ produces $L\to L'$. Restrictions compose as restrictions, so the maps and higher simplices commute with evaluation and changes of weight. A strict enriched cone with vertex $B$ is an object of the right-hand cone category and thus yields the required enriched functor. The enlargement lemma ensures that $F$ and all its old simplices remain the given strict representatives throughout this calculation.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text: For any small coherent diagram of complete enriched categories, [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability] computes its limit in algebroids with object space the limit of object spaces and mapping objects $\lim_iE_i(x_i,y_i)$ at compatible objects. By [lem-coef-algebroid-completion], complete objects are the local objects for its single map; [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] says that the inclusion of this local subcategory computes its limits in the ambient category. This is consequently also the complete-enriched-category limit. Its composition is the unique map whose projection to each factor is that factor's composition after the two projections; identities and every higher operation are induced by the same projections. The operadic equations follow after these projections, by the universal property of the limit. This proves the mapping-object claim for all the products, pullbacks and inverse limits used above.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text:
Fix $v\in\mathcal V$. The crossing lemma [lem-coef-collage-crossing-transformations] supplies the coherent mapping-object functor $\mathcal E(-,-):(U\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}}\times U\mathcal E\to\mathcal V$ induced by enriched composition and units; composing it with the coherent Hom bifunctor [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] of $\mathcal V$ at $v$ gives
$$H_v(x,y)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,\mathcal E(x,y))$$
as a coherent space-valued functor on $(U\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}}\times U\mathcal E$; its actions are precomposition and postcomposition with all unit and composition simplices. Form its ordinary infinity-categorical collage $C_v$ by [lem-coef-space-bimodule-collage]. The fixed-end crossing lemma [lem-coef-collage-crossing-transformations] identifies the space of coefficient-parametrized enriched transformations with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(S,C_v)}(P_0,Q_1)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,\mathcal E^S(P,Q)).$$
The coefficient probe is the free algebroid on one $v$-labeled edge, supplied by [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability], with endpoints fixed. Complete this probe using [lem-coef-algebroid-completion], whose localization unit supplies the completed object; tensoring that completed probe with $S_{\mathcal V}$ uses the tensor/cotensor adjunction. The forward map records the crossing label for each mixed string and the inverse glues those compatible labels. Faces at the crossing are exactly the two actions of $H_v$; the other faces and degeneracies are the diagram operations. The crossing lemma includes all parameter simplices, so this is natural in $v$ and endpoint diagrams without testing only tensor-unit sections.

source.place: Sections 5.1.1-5.1.8 and 5.2.2-5.2.7; agent enriched refinement using the cited tensor calculus and algebroid limit statements.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula] to the two diagrams $P_0,Q_1:S\to C_v$. Their mixed mapping spaces are $H_v(Ps,Qt)$ by the collage statement used in step 9. Consequently step 9 gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,E^S(P,Q))\simeq\lim_{(s\to t)\in\operatorname{Tw}(S)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,E(Ps,Qt)).$$
The index and its source-target functor are exactly [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Presentability gives the small limit of $E(Ps,Qt)$ in $\mathcal V$. Representables preserve this limit and the Yoneda criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] now gives the asserted equivalence of objects of $\mathcal V$, since the comparison above holds naturally for every $v$. Evaluation at $1_s$ is the component projection by the coherent-end theorem. Composing two transformations is componentwise composition; projecting the two descriptions to each mixed mapping object gives the same composite. The same argument for identities and higher composition simplices proves their compatibility. Its parameter naturality is already present in the collage, cotensor and coherent-end comparisons. For a simplicial shape use its freely generated infinity-category, as stipulated by the tensor calculus.

source.place: Example 8.3.4.22, applied to the ordinary collage of the coefficient probe; agent Yoneda argument recovering the V-valued object.

proof.text: Finally closedness gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(a,[v,\lim_iM_i])\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(a\otimes v,\lim_iM_i)\simeq\lim_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(a\otimes v,M_i)\simeq\lim_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(a,[v,M_i])$. The representable limit and Yoneda criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identify this with $[v,\lim_iM_i]\simeq\lim_i[v,M_i]$. This includes empty limits. Every probe and tensor product in this proof belongs to the coefficient category or to the tensor product of enriched categories; at no point was an object tensor in $F(j)$ required.
